rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent massing idea in all four views: a bent, low bar with a capped/stepped upper profile. The silhouette is reasonably resolved and the geometry does not visibly collide across views, so repair integrity is acceptable. However, for neighborhood living the visible mass is too sealed and too object-like at the ground. The verified access edge is not answered by a legible public void, court, notch, or undercut; instead the mass sits off the frontage with little semantic engagement. The section also feels weak for the brief: the upper bent/cantilevered condition creates some hierarchy, but it does not clearly reinforce an active ground threshold or a public/shared open space. The form is closer to a compact sculpted block than a street-building with an explicit active edge, so program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A single dominant mass can be legible even when lightly stepped or capped, but the upper profile should stay subordinate to the main bar logic.
